attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post.

semantics.note: Faithful paraphrase. It is a firm, evaluative statement about where OpenAI's value lay up to publication.

contract.note: The plain reading (staff made up substantially all of the value; the listed assets had little independent value) is the ordinary meaning of the words. Requiring a split of value between staff and assets is demanding, but it is what the claim implies.

evidence.note: Microsoft's Jan 2023 disclosure shows its deal covered technology and commercialisation rights. It does not put a value on those assets separately from the staff, so it neither supports nor contradicts.

reviews.rationale: The packet has no valuation or transaction that splits OpenAI's value between its workforce and its IP, data, customers or infrastructure. The only item is a company disclosure, which counts as context. The evidence available does not settle the claim either way.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post.

semantics.note: Mostly faithful. 'Inevitably conflict' is a bit stronger than 'never going to have a perfect relationship', but 'ticking time bomb' does imply that conflict was built in.

contract.note: Using the Nov 2023 crisis as the main test fits Marcus's own mention of 'the recent drama'. The contract fairly says that inevitability cannot be shown from a single instance.

evidence.note: The board's own announcement shows a serious conflict, but gives lack of candour as the reason, not profit versus safety.
Op-ed by two former directors (Toner, McCauley) saying profit pressure undermined self-governance. It is a participant's interpretation, not an independent finding.
OpenAI's summary of the WilmerHale review says the firing did not arise from safety or finance concerns but from lost trust. It is a company disclosure, not the full record.

reviews.rationale: The evidence conflicts. Former directors say profit pressure was behind the crisis; OpenAI's summary of its investigation says it was about lost trust, not safety or finances. Neither independently establishes the cause, and one episode cannot show the conflict was inevitable. The evidence available does not settle the claim.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post.

semantics.note: Faithful paraphrase of a retrospective description of OpenAI's strength.

contract.note: In context, 'new paradigm' means replacing the underlying approach. Reading it as architectural replacement, rather than every training improvement, is the ordinary and fair reading.

evidence.note: The original Transformer paper, with mainly Google affiliations.
The GPT-3 paper credits scaling with major performance gains.
The GPT-4 report says the model is Transformer-based, with infrastructure built to work predictably across scales.
OpenAI's human-feedback training work (InstructGPT) shows contributions beyond scale, but it does not replace the Transformer approach.

reviews.rationale: Under the contract's reading, the claim holds. The Transformer came from Google research, OpenAI's main GPT advances kept that architecture, and OpenAI's own papers put scaling at the centre. The human-feedback training work qualifies how sweeping the claim sounds, but it is not a replacement paradigm.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post.

semantics.note: Close paraphrase. It drops 'a lot of companies spent money testing' but keeps the core clauses.

contract.note: Reading 'this year' as approximate calendar-2023 revenue, profit as unclear at publication, and 'few' as a small minority without a set cutoff is fair and ordinary.

evidence.note: Predibase survey, May–Jul 2023: about 14% of respondents had LLMs in production, 44% were only experimenting. Small sample, not shown to be representative, no spending data.
OpenAI's own 2026 statement that it reached $1B revenue within a year of launch. The period is too loose to confirm realized calendar-2023 revenue.
The 80% Fortune 500 figure counts registered accounts, not production use.
Confirms the survey was public in Aug 2023; it is not a second sample.

reviews.rationale: The adoption clause has partial support from one small survey that is not shown to be representative. No source gives realized calendar-2023 revenue, and nothing shows what profit information was public at the time. The evidence available does not settle the claim as a whole.
